content.text: I have reviewed every fee, termination, remedy, and general-provisions clause. No Customer-payable liquidated damages, penalty, or minimum termination charge exists anywhere.

input.quote: NO DAMAGES FOR TERMINATION. NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR DAMAGES OF ANY KIND, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES, DAMAGES FOR THE LOSS OF GOODWILL, PROSPECTIVE PROFITS OR ANTICIPATED INCOME, OR DAMAGES RESULTING FROM ANY EXPENDITURES, INVESTMENTS, LEASES OR COMMITMENTS MADE BY EITHER PARTY ON ACCOUNT OF THE TERMINATION OR EXPIRATION OF THIS AGREEMENT IN ACCORDANCE WITH ITS TERMS.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination/minimum fee on us. Article XXIII (p0142) expressly provides that neither party is liable for damages of any kind on account of termination or expiration, and Article XXI's effect-of-termination provision (p0138) requires only return of Licensed Technology, with no exit payment. The payment mechanics we checked are ordinary consideration, not liquidated amounts: the volume-band user fees and the accrual floor tied to actual recorded trading (p0070), the $2,500 monthly support fee, the audit-cost shift if a discrepancy over 5% is found (p0064), and Licensor's retained right on immediate termination to receive payments "for all trades performed using the Licensed Technology" (p0049) — i.e., fees already earned, not accelerated or unearned remaining contract value. This meets the preferred position (Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties), so no redline is proposed.
